name: table-count
description: Number of Drizzle pgTable() definitions across shared/. The mature-machine north star is a SMALLER schema (<=450 tables); today's count is far above it. This strict down-only ratchet makes the schema monotonic: adding a table fails CI until the baseline is deliberately bumped (a conscious 'yes we need this'), and every consolidation lowers the baseline toward the target. Founder-chosen 'strict' 2026-07-16.
lastBumpNote: 757 -> 758 on 2026-08-12: decision_snapshots -- Decision Memory's durable boundary (Master Audit BI20). Earned by a law, not a feature. Without it every recorded decision reads against LIVE rows, so a decision silently changes meaning when the data behind it changes -- BL3's 'historical decision fidelity' fitness function, one of only TWO classified fully `unenforced` in shared/architecture/canon.ts, whose fail condition is stated verbatim as 'a prior decision changes meaning when current data or Pack rules change'. One row freezes what was KNOWN at decision time: resolved evidence WITH the claim ids behind it (so an auditor can re-read those exact claims, re-run resolution at the recorded evidence_as_of under the recorded resolution_policy_version, and confirm the frozen answer follows from them), the assumptions in force AND their origin (a rent figure the customer typed is a different kind of thing from one a Strategy Pack defaulted -- conflating them is how a platform default silently becomes 'what the customer believed'), the alternatives considered and why each lost, the unknowns accepted, who decided under what authority, and the Strategy Pack id+version in force (BI91 -- updating a Pack must not silently reinterpret historical decisions). The unknowns field is DERIVED from the evidence rather than asked of the caller, because the honest half of a decision record is exactly what a hurried caller omits; it is how law 3 (unknown and conflict are valid states) carries forward into Decision Memory. WHY NOT REUSE AN EXISTING TABLE: the repo already had FOURTEEN decision-shaped tables (board_decisions, ceo_decision_replays, decisions_inbox_items, decision_patterns, solene_decisions, solene_decision_traces, solene_pre_call_decisions, ...) and every one is FOUNDER/autopilot control-plane state -- queues of things needing the founder, traces of the autopilot's own reasoning. None records a CUSTOMER's investment decision and none freezes its inputs; reusing one would make Founder OS the owner of customer investment truth, which BI5 forbids explicitly. WHY NOT A JSONB COLUMN ON deals: because a `pass` -- the most under-recorded and most valuable decision an investor makes -- happens when no deal exists and never will, so hanging Decision Memory off deals would lose exactly the decisions worth remembering. IMMUTABLE BY CONTRACT: no updated_at column, no UPDATE/DELETE path in the store, and no PUT/PATCH/DELETE endpoint -- later evidence and later outcomes append context, nothing edits a snapshot (laws 6 and 9). subject_id carries NO foreign key because a snapshot must SURVIVE its subject; organization_id does cascade, so customer-data deletion stays complete.
